card.band: 8 h. Buckets: transports, lifecycle, tool translation, chat-loop integration, commands, errors. A frontier agent covers stdio and basic calls but misses protocol edge cases such as notifications, cancellation, pagination and timeouts. A weaker model fails the integration.
card.cheat: Faking tool calls without a real protocol exchange fails the mock servers, which check the exact messages. The hidden servers are not shipped.
card.grading: Hidden pytest tests drive the public Coder and CLI with scripted mock MCP servers and a fake model. They check the JSON-RPC handshake, tool schemas passed to the model, call results, error handling and config parsing. The existing suite is a regression gate. Score is the fraction passed.
card.reference: Our own implementation, about 1.5-2.5k lines. It scores 1 on the hidden tests.
card.task: Add an MCP client to aider covering stdio and streamable HTTP transports, tool discovery, tool-call execution inside the chat loop, per-server config and /mcp commands. It must work offline against local mock servers.
card.title: Model Context Protocol client and tool loop for aider

history: Real open issue #2525 and a real MCP spec, but the whole grading surface is our own 60-150 hand-written mock-server tests, and the config keys, /mcp subcommands and tool naming are interface choices we would invent, so other valid designs fail. facts.claim: Aider issue #2525 exists, is open, and requests MCP support (opened 2024-12-03, label enhancement)
Aider latest release is v0.86.0, and no release note from v0.77.0 to v0.86.0 mentions MCP
PR #3672 'Add MCP support' (stdio only, rough) is closed and not merged (closed Jul 4 2025 after its head repo was deleted)
PR #3937 'Add MCP Support with LiteLLM' (stdio only, LiteLLM bridge, per-request connections) is closed and not merged (closed 2025-11-25)
A community fork (aider-ce) incorporates PR #3937 and adds streamable HTTP transport support, so public code covering part of the scope exists outside upstream

MCP spec 2025-06-18 defines two standard transports: stdio (newline-delimited JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout) and Streamable HTTP (single endpoint with POST and GET, SSE, Mcp-Session-Id, MCP-Protocol-Version headers)
Seed smoke_build is empty: no offline build or test-suite probe was run, so build cost and suite determinism are unverified

spike_plan.kill_if: The suite is non-deterministic, or the chat loop cannot take a tool result without a large rewrite of the Coder core (more than 1 day of work).
spike_plan.pass_if: Suite runs green offline in under 10 minutes, the stdio round trip works end to end with a fake model, and the message log is identical across 5 runs.
steps: Clone the pinned head 5dc9490 into a scratch container with network; check that the existing pytest suite runs offline and record its pass count and any flakiness across 3 runs (also resolves the empty smoke_build).
Check whether the mcp Python SDK is installed in the image; if not, confirm the agent must hand-roll JSON-RPC (decide whether to ship it or not).
Write a 60-line stdio mock MCP server answering initialize, tools/list and tools/call, and check it with a raw subprocess JSON-RPC exchange.
Write a scripted fake model that returns one tool call, then run one aider chat turn in the test harness with the mock server attached; check that the tool result returns to the model.
Check determinism: run the same scripted turn 5 times and confirm identical message logs.

Read PR #3937 diff only for the config schema and fork's streamable HTTP approach, to decide what the task text must specify (config keys, flags, /mcp subcommands, tool naming) so hidden tests don't encode one internal structure.

v1.summary: The seed is real and sealable: aider issue #2525 is open, Apache-2.0, and MCP is not merged upstream, though closed PR #3672, closed PR #3937 and the aider-ce fork give partial public lookup, so the snapshot must exclude all history. Before build, the task text must pin config keys, CLI flags, /mcp subcommands and tool naming, and the smoke build must be run because it is empty and build cost is unknown.

v2.note: Real open issue #2525 and a real MCP spec, but the whole grading surface is our own 60-150 hand-written mock-server tests, and the config keys, /mcp subcommands and tool naming are interface choices we would invent, so other valid designs fail. Aider has no native tool-call loop, so the hidden tests must encode one integration shape. Public partial code exists (closed PRs #3672 and #3937, the aider-ce fork with streamable HTTP), and MCP clients are well known to frontier models (frontier_hours 6), so this also leans K8. No smoke build.
